title: Profiling and Benchmarking
learning_outcomes: Explain what profiling and benchmarking contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: profilers.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Performance work starts with a measurable target and representative workload. Profile before changing code, compare the same conditions after a change, and consider memory, cache invalidation, and regression risk. In this lesson, focus on profilers; then compare it with benchmark methodology. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use profiling and benchmarking when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Performance work starts with a measurable target and representative workload. Profile before changing code, compare the same conditions after a change, and consider memory, cache invalidation, and regression risk. For profiling and benchmarking, begin with profilers. Also distinguish benchmark methodology; identifying bottlenecks; representative test workloads. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

items.title: Profilers
items.text: Check the operation result, use a known storage boundary, and consider empty files, permissions, invalid paths, and cleanup.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Measure a representative workload before optimization, then repeat the measurement and watch for regressions.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for profiling and benchmarking from top to bottom. Start by identifying profilers, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

content.task: Create a second small example for profiling and benchmarking that demonstrates "profilers". Before running it, write down the expected result and one boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example includes a clear use of profilers.
The learner can explain its input, rule, and observable output.
At least one edge case is tested or documented.
hints: Start with the most direct listed subtopic and a single input.
Keep the example small enough that you can predict the output manually.
Test one normal case and one empty, invalid, or boundary case.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.

summary: Profiling and Benchmarking is one part of the PHP implementation workflow.
Prefer explicit behavior and testable examples over implicit assumptions.
Measure a representative workload before optimization, then repeat the measurement and watch for regressions.
